_readme: Cost reference for FleetSense Layer 3. Plain data, deliberately not code -- a
maintenance engineer should be able to update these figures without touching Python.
labour_rates_eur_per_hour  hourly rates used to derive the labour part of a job
repair_jobs                the actual remedial actions, each with a cost BAND
locations                  the 9 fault locations FleetSense can detect, each
pointing at the repair_job that fixes it
Why locations map to jobs rather than carrying their own prices: bearing_outer,
bearing_inner and bearing_ball are three detections of ONE physical bearing. They
share a single job id, so a file flagging all three still costs one bearing job, not
three. Summing per-location costs would report ~3x the real figure.
Jobs marked action='replace' supersede action='repair' jobs: if a broken rotor bar
sends you to a new motor you do not additionally pay to change its bearings. The
consuming code is responsible for that resolution.
Costs are BANDS, never point values. Two reasons: real quotes vary by shop, and
FleetSense's own presence_confidence values are RandomForest vote fractions, not
calibrated probabilities -- so a single precise euro figure would imply a certainty

Each job carries both a `label` (short noun phrase, used when one job is referenced from another, e.g. 'Already included in Bearing renewal and realignment') and a `statement` (formal sentence, used as the headline on a flagged issue). Keeping both avoids sentences reading badly when nested inside other sentences.

meta.market_warning: These are Romanian market prices expressed in EUR, NOT EU-wide figures. Converting the currency does not make them portable: labour rates in Western Europe run several times higher (a Romanian shop rate of ~EUR 16-30/h compares with EUR 80-120/h in Germany or Austria). Parts prices travel well; labour does not. Re-source the labour_rates block before using this outside Romania.
meta.fx_rate_used: 1 EUR = 5.0 RON (approximate; RON is a loosely managed float against EUR and has sat near 4.95-5.10 for several years)
meta.vat_note: Romanian retail prices quoted include TVA at 19%. The rewind figure is explicitly VAT-inclusive (520 RON incl. / 430 RON excl.).
meta.motor_under_analysis: 2.2 kW three-phase asynchronous induction motor, 2-pole (pole-pairs = 1, confirmed from the measured electrical fundamental). Bearing type SKF 6205-2Z/C3, named in the MCC5-THU dataset paper.
known_gaps: Romanian motor rewinding shops overwhelmingly do not publish prices -- the usual answer is 'preturile sunt negociabile pentru fiecare lucrare in parte'. The rewind figure below is one shop's published rate, not a market average.
shaft_repair has no published Romanian price anywhere I could find; its band is derived from shop labour hours only. It is the least trustworthy line here and is marked confidence 'low'.
The published rewind service is quoted for motors up to 2 kW. This motor is 2.2 kW, marginally above that bracket.

motor_workshop.note: Derived from Romanian electrician rates: 80-130 RON/h in major cities, 100-150 RON/h in Bucharest.

authorised_electrician.note: ANRE-authorised rate, 100-200 RON/h. Emergency or out-of-hours work carries a 30-50% premium not modelled here.

breakdown.parts_detail: 2 x SKF 6205-2Z/C3 at EUR 4 each (19.95 RON). Bearings are replaced in pairs: the second bearing has seen identical service hours and replacing one alone invites a repeat teardown.

stator_rewind.label: Rewind stator

breakdown.parts_detail: All-in shop price. The published service covers rewinding to manufacturer spec, bearing replacement and varnishing, with a 6-month warranty -- so it already absorbs bearing_replacement.

stator_rewind.economic_note: Borderline for this motor. Against a budget 2-pole replacement (EUR 145) a rewind is ~72% of new-motor cost, which exceeds the ~57% industry rule of thumb and argues for replacement. Against a better-specified motor (EUR 405) the same rewind is ~26% and clearly worth doing. The verdict genuinely depends on which motor you would buy to replace it.

breakdown.parts_detail: EUR 145 = budget 2-pole 2.2 kW (723 RON, Gamak AGM2E 90 L 2, 2880 rpm, IP55, 83% efficiency). EUR 405 = higher-specified 4-pole unit (2023.92 RON). The motor under analysis is 2-pole, so the lower end is the honest comparator. Excludes removal/refitting labour.

shaft_repair.label: Straighten or re-machine shaft
shaft_repair.statement: The shaft requires straightening or re-machining

breakdown.parts_detail: Machine-shop work. A replacement shaft, where straightening is not viable, pushes this toward the motor_replacement band and the two should be compared.

shaft_repair.confidence_note: No published Romanian price found for shaft straightening. Derived from workshop labour hours alone -- treat as an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a quote.

airgap_correction.label: Bearing renewal and realignment
airgap_correction.statement: The bearings require renewal and the end shields realignment

breakdown.parts_detail: Eccentricity is a condition of the rotor-stator air gap rather than a failed component. It is corrected by renewing worn bearings and re-seating/realigning the end shields; severe cases with core rub are motor_replacement instead.

airgap_correction.confidence_note: Derived from parts plus workshop labour; no single published line item covers this job.

supply_investigation.label: Investigate and correct supply imbalance
supply_investigation.statement: The supply imbalance requires investigation and correction

breakdown.parts_detail: No motor parts. This is switchgear/cabling/transformer-side work.

supply_investigation.important: This is NOT a motor repair. Voltage unbalance originates upstream of the motor; dispatching a motor workshop would fix nothing while the real fault keeps damaging the machine. It belongs to a different trade and a different budget line, and should be reported separately from motor repair cost.

bearing_outer.label: Bearing - outer race
bearing_outer.note: FleetSense does not identify which end (drive or non-drive) the fault sits on; both bearings are replaced regardless, so this does not affect cost.

rotor_bar.label: Broken rotor bar
rotor_bar.note: Bar repair (welding/brazing replacement bars to the end rings) is a real service, quoted internationally at EUR 2800-14000, but it applies to large motors with fabricated copper cages. A 2.2 kW motor has a cast-aluminium cage, which industry guidance treats as non-repairable at any size -- replacement is the only sensible action.

winding.label: Stator winding
winding.note: See the stator_rewind economic_note: rewind versus replace is genuinely borderline for a motor this small.

profiairvent_rewind.what: Rewind of an electric motor up to 2 kW: 520 RON incl. VAT (430 excl.). Covers rewinding to manufacturer spec, bearing replacement, varnishing. 6-month warranty.

rulmentika_6205.what: SKF 6205-2Z/C3 deep groove ball bearing, 25x52x15 mm: 19.95 RON, in stock. This is the exact bearing named in the MCC5-THU dataset paper.

dedeman_motor.what: Gamak AGM2E 90 L 2, 2.2 kW / 3 CP three-phase, 2-pole, 2880 rpm, IP55, 83% efficiency: 723.00 RON.

electrician_rates_bucuresti.what: Romanian electrician hourly rates 2026: 100-150 RON/h Bucharest, 80-130 RON/h other major cities, 50-100 RON/h smaller towns; ANRE-authorised 100-200 RON/h.

daibau_electrician.what: Independent 2026 Romanian labour price guide for electrical work, used to cross-check the rates above.

industrialmonitor_repair_replace.what: Repair-vs-replace thresholds; rotor bar repair costs and the guidance that failed cast-aluminium rotor bars warrant replacement at any size.

universalrewind_repair_replace.what: Motors under ~15 HP are typically not repaired because minimum repair cost exceeds the ~57% threshold of a new motor's price.

repairengineering_shaft.what: Shaft straightening as a service; background for the shaft_repair estimate. No Romanian pricing published.
